summary: Misunas's report is an edited, summarized transcript of talks at a July 1977 MIT workshop on data-flow computers and program organization. For this survey its relevant content is architectural: partitioned instruction memories, packet communication between modules, and dynamic assignment of instructions or tasks to processors, with almost nothing on compiler-generated communication.
why_read: It is an early record of data-flow machine proposals, showing how instructions and tasks were assigned to processors and how results moved between modules.
main_contribution: It records the status of several 1977 data-flow projects, covering machine organizations, languages, simulators and performance analysis.
main_limitation: The report is a heavily edited summary of talks, and one speaker states that efficient Fortran-to-data-flow translation would be very difficult.
evaluation_method: simulators and analytic bounds reported in talks; no controlled comparison
states_relationship_to: Kosinski's data flow language for operating systems
notes: Title, first author and year match the catalog and the cover and title page: 'Report on the Workshop on Data Flow Computer and Program Organization', David P. Misunas, November 1977, MIT/LCS/TM-92 (the cover prints the title in capitals; the front matter uses title case). The PDF has 53 pages, not the 54 stated in the brief. Individual talks are by their speakers; Misunas compiled and edited the transcripts. The text layer is error-prone OCR, so claims are paraphrased. Page citations are the report's printed page numbers (PDF page minus 3), which match its table of contents.
